summary: A hard step change took auth-service from ~0.2% to a flat ~36% 401 invalid_token error rate with onset between 14:00Z and 14:02Z, and it has persisted through 15:54Z. The two 14:00–14:01Z changes are the only ones in scope and both plausibly target token validation: deploy dep-5710 (jjwt 0.11→0.12 breaking parser API + TokenValidator rewrite) at 14:00Z and signing-key rotation cfg-2705 (jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10→k-2026-04) at 14:01Z. The ranking is genuinely close — H1 key rotation at 0.42 versus H2 deploy regression at 0.40 — and each maps to a near-identical real precedent (HIST-108 and HIST-109, respectively), so we cannot separate them with the evidence available. The outcome is therefore inconclusive: neither change was reverted, auth-service logs are unsearchable, and no per-replica or per-caller breakdown exists to prove the partial failure domain that the flat ~36% plateau implies. Safe mitigations plus a discriminating test are the right next step.

ranked_hypotheses.title: JWT signing-key rotation (cfg-2705) published new key id before all auth-service pods loaded the new JWKS key
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The scheduled signing-key rotation cfg-2705 changed jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04 at 14:01Z, one minute after the JWT library deploy. Pods that had not yet refreshed the key/JWKS continued to validate against the old (or a mismatched) key material, so assertions signed with one key id were rejected by replicas holding the other — a partial failure domain producing a flat ~36% 401 invalid_token plateau with unchanged latency, CPU, and throttling. Origin: auth-service signing-key configuration change.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2705 rotates jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 at 14:01Z

Not all auth-service pods load the new key/JWKS atomically, so a subset of replicas validate against stale or mismatched key material (same mechanism as HIST-108: key id published before all pods loaded JWKS)
Tokens signed/verified against one key id are rejected by replicas holding the other, yielding 401 invalid_token
Only the subset of replicas/keys out of sync fails, giving a flat ~36% (roughly one-third) error plateau rather than whole-fleet failure
No latency, CPU, or throttle change accompanies the error step, consistent with a key-mismatch rejection path rather than overload

assumptions: Pods do not atomically reload the rotated key; a stale-key window exists (not verifiable — auth-service logs unsearchable, no per-replica metric)
cfg-2705 actually took effect on validation paths at ~14:01Z
The ~36% plateau maps to a key/replica subset rather than a caller subset — per-replica and per-caller splits were never obtained

ranked_hypotheses.title: auth-service deploy dep-5710 (jjwt 0.11->0.12 + TokenValidator rewrite) introduced a validation regression rejecting valid tokens
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-5710, deployed at 14:00Z with the breaking jjwt parser API change and a rewritten TokenValidator, changed the runtime semantics of token validation (e.g. clock-skew/leeway default, claim validation, audience/issuer check), so a fraction of legitimately valid tokens now fail verification with 401 invalid_token. Origin: auth-service code release. The fraction (~36%) would reflect the subset of tokens that rely on the changed semantics.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 deploys jjwt 0.11->0.12 (breaking parser API) and a rewritten TokenValidator at 14:00Z
The parser rewrite changes validation semantics (per HIST-109, an auth library upgrade changed the clock-skew default and broke token validation)
A subset of tokens that previously passed now fail verification -> 401 invalid_token at ~36%
Error step appears in the 14:00->14:02 bucket, i.e. immediately after the 14:00Z deploy
No latency/CPU/throttle change: the failures are semantic rejections, not resource stalls

assumptions: The rewritten validator actually rejects valid tokens at ~1/3 rate rather than 0% or 100%
Onset bucket granularity (2-min) does not hide a symptom start before 14:00Z
No client-side token-format change explains the fraction

ranked_hypotheses.title: Fault originates outside auth-service: api-gateway/caller or shared redis-cache path corrupts or drops tokens so auth-service correctly rejects them
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service is behaving correctly; an upstream caller (api-gateway) or the shared redis-cache path mangles, truncates, or drops tokens (or serves stale session state) for roughly a third of requests, so auth-service legitimately returns 401 invalid_token. Origin: a component upstream of or shared with auth-service. This contradicts the reporter's assumption that auth-service is broken.

causal_chain.claim: api-gateway calls auth-service for validation (auth-service is 'called by api-gateway')
api-gateway routing/header handling (or a deploy there) alters or truncates Authorization material for a subset of callers
auth-service receives malformed/invalid tokens and correctly rejects them with 401 invalid_token
redis-cache is the only shared component in the graph and 0 config changes were seen for it, a possible alternate corruption/staleness origin but with no observed change

assumptions: An api-gateway deploy or routing change near 14:00Z exists but was never queried (budget exhausted) — no finding supports it
Caller-side token mutation at ~1/3 rate is possible without any recorded change
The error step at 14:00-14:02 may be coincidental to the step at 14:00Z rather than caused by it

ranked_hypotheses.title: Identity log-pipeline outage and the 401s share a common credential/config/network change this morning
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The identity-namespace log pipeline has been down since the morning and the 401s began at 14:00Z; a single credential, secret, certificate or network/config change could have broken both log shipping and token signing/key distribution. Alternatively the 401s are a real but separate fault amplified in perception because missing logs prevent diagnosis. Origin: an unidentified shared control-plane/credential change, not the 14:00Z auth-service changes.

causal_chain.claim: Identity log pipeline down since the morning, before the 14:00Z auth changes
A shared credential/secret/config change breaks both log shipping and token/key operations
Token validation fails for a subset of requests, producing 401 invalid_token

assumptions: A shared change exists — untested: 'logging' is not a known service, get_config_changes(logging) returned not_found, and no logging node exists in the auth-service graph
Log-pipeline outage precedes onset by hours, so the two would have to be linked by a delayed mechanism, not a single 14:00Z event

ranked_hypotheses.title: Clock skew / NTP drift or resource exhaustion on a subset of auth-service nodes
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A subset of auth-service instances suffer NTP/clock drift (failing JWT nbf/exp checks) or resource exhaustion (OOM/throttle) so a fraction of requests fail with 401. Origin: infrastructure/time-sync rather than a code or config change.

causal_chain.claim: A subset of nodes drifts in time or runs out of memory/CPU
Drifted replicas fail nbf/exp validation (or exhausted replicas error/restart), returning 401 for ~1/3 of traffic

assumptions: Clock skew could exist on a subset of nodes but no NTP or per-replica metric exists to show it
Exhaustion would normally raise latency/CPU — flat p99 and flat cpu_pct argue against it

facts.statement: auth-service deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0) went live at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z, carrying a breaking JWT parser API change (jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12) and a rewritten TokenValidator.
Scheduled signing-key rotation cfg-2705 changed auth-service config jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04 at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z, one minute after the deploy.

Both changes in the 14:00–14:01Z window touch token validation/signing material, and they are the only deployments and only config change in scope for the whole 2026-04-14T00:00Z–2026-04-15T15:59Z window across all services (deployments count=2, config changes count=1).

The auth-service error rate sits at baseline ~0.2% at 14:00:00Z and jumps to 37.21% avg (max 38.34) in the next 2-minute bucket at 14:02:00Z, then holds ~35–37% for the rest of the window — a step change with onset between 14:00 and 14:02.
The 6-minute-bucket view localizes onset to the 14:00:00Z bucket (avg 24.84%, max 38.34%) versus 13:54:00Z (avg 0.25%), and the plateau is ~36% (mean ~36.2% per 6-min bucket) at least through 15:54.
Request rate is unchanged across onset (~386–412 req/s before and after), so the error jump is not traffic-driven.
Latency p99 stays flat at ~88–92 ms across onset, arguing against resource/saturation-driven timeouts.
CPU (~37.4–38.6% in every 15-min bucket 13:00–15:45) and rate-limit counters (~1.75–2.18/min) are flat across onset — no saturation or throttle signal at 14:00.
Neither candidate change was reverted: dep-5710 shows status live with rolled_back_at null, and cfg-2705 has no rollback/revert entry, as of the latest data.

Historical precedent HIST-108 (2025-10-01) matches the exact symptom set and cfg-2705's mechanism: '401s after JWT signing key rotation', root cause 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS', resolved by re-publishing the previous key and staging the rotation.

Historical precedent HIST-109 (2025-07-11) parallels dep-5710: 'Token validation regression after auth library upgrade', root cause 'JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default', resolved by rollback and pinning the skew config.
Both matching auth precedents were resolved by reverting the triggering change; in this incident neither candidate was reverted.

auth-service's dependency graph calls user-db, redis-cache (the only shared:true component, with 0 config changes in the window), kyc-provider, and is called by api-gateway; no per-replica metric exists in available_metrics (cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, rate_limited_per_min, request_rate, restarts).

No historical precedent links a logging/observability pipeline outage to auth or token-validation failures, and no logging/observability node exists in the auth-service dependency graph or in the known-services list.

auth-service error_rate still at baseline ~0.21% (max 0.26) in the 14:00:00Z reading; request rate ~399 req/s and latency p99 ~90 ms stay flat.
Scheduled signing-key rotation cfg-2705 changes jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04, applied by security-automation — one minute after the deploy.

Incident INC-007 (SEV-1) reported: ~one third of token validations fail with 401 invalid_token; auth-service error rate 36%; identity-namespace log pipeline already down since morning so auth-service logs are unsearchable.
Error rate holds a flat ~36% plateau (mean ~36.2% per 6-min bucket) with unchanged request rate, latency, CPU and throttling — partial failure domain signature.

Latest data: neither dep-5710 nor cfg-2705 has been rolled back or reverted; auth-service still calls user-db, redis-cache (only shared component, 0 config changes) and kyc-provider, and is called by api-gateway.

recommended_actions.action: Stop the scheduled rotation from advancing and re-publish/restore the previous signing key material (revert config jwt.signing.key_id from k-2026-04 back to k-2025-10, i.e. roll back cfg-2705) on auth-service, then force a key/JWKS reload across all replicas.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2705 (jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 at 14:01Z) is the top-ranked hypothesis and matches HIST-108 exactly, whose documented resolution was 'Re-published previous key; staged rotation'. A key-id flip is cheap, reversible and does not require a code change.

recommended_actions.action: In parallel, if the error rate does not drop within one observation bucket after the key revert, roll back dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0) to the previous release to restore the pre-rewrite TokenValidator and jjwt version.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 (confidence 0.40) is statistically indistinguishable from H1 and matches HIST-109, whose resolution was a rollback. Because neither change was ever reverted (F4/F15), neither mechanism has been excluded; reverting the second candidate is the fastest discrimination path. Order the two reverts so the cheaper config change is tested first.

recommended_actions.action: Before/while reverting, capture the discriminating evidence with the remaining budget: query per-instance/replica error_rate for auth-service (or add a temporary per-replica error breakdown) and a per-caller breakdown of the failing requests at api-gateway.
recommended_actions.rationale: The flat ~36% plateau implies a partial failure domain (a key/replica subset or a caller subset) but this was never proven; splitting the failure by replica vs caller is exactly what separates H1 (key/replica subset) from H3 (upstream caller subset).

recommended_actions.action: Restore log searchability for the identity namespace (fix or bypass the log pipeline) and re-query auth-service logs for JWKS/key-loading errors vs token-parse/claim-validation errors in the 14:00–14:15Z window.
recommended_actions.rationale: The single mechanism-level discriminator between H1 and H2 is log-level and is currently unavailable; every hypothesis is capped at low confidence precisely because auth-service logs cannot be searched.

recommended_actions.action: After the error rate returns to baseline, re-run the key rotation as a staged rollout: publish the new key id, verify all pods have loaded the new JWKS, then cut signing over — and verify the jjwt 0.12 validator against a replay corpus of real tokens (clock-skew/leeway, claim, audience/issuer checks) before re-deploying v7.3.0.
recommended_actions.rationale: Both HIST-108 ('staged rotation') and HIST-109 ('pinned skew config') were fixed by making the change safe rather than merely reverting it; either candidate change remains the likely driver until disproven.

recommended_actions.action: Add per-replica and per-key-id validation metrics (JWKS load state, key id in use per pod, 401 reason-code breakdown) and alerting on auth-service 401 invalid_token rate.
recommended_actions.rationale: The absence of any per-replica metric in available_metrics (only cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, rate_limited_per_min, request_rate, restarts) is why the partial-failure-domain reading of the ~36% plateau could not be confirmed. Response was also delayed ~11–12 minutes from onset to report.

recommended_actions.action: Decouple auth-service observability from the identity-namespace log pipeline (or add an independent log/ship path and a canary on log delivery) so that a logging outage cannot blind auth investigations.
recommended_actions.rationale: The logging outage demonstrably blocked log-based triage in this incident; no logging component is even present in the auth-service dependency graph or known-services list, so this blind spot is structural.

data_gaps: auth-service logs are unsearchable (identity-namespace log pipeline down since the morning), so no log-level signature of the 401s exists — the JWKS stale-key mechanism (H1) and the parser-regression mechanism (H2) cannot be distinguished from logs.
auth-service exposes no per-replica/instance metric, so the ~36% error rate cannot be split by replica and the partial-fleet hypothesis is unproven.
No per-caller breakdown of the failing traffic was obtained, so it is unknown whether failures are uniform across callers or concentrated in a subset (H3 remains untested).

get_deployments for api-gateway and get_config_changes for auth-service were never executed (tool-call budget exhausted), so an api-gateway routing deploy or additional auth-service config flips near 14:00–14:02Z cannot be ruled out.
No precise time-alignment of the 401 onset against the 14:00Z deploy and 14:01Z key rotation was measured; only the ~14:12Z report time and the bucketed error series are available.

Neighbor services could not be queried ('gateway' and 'user-service' returned not_found), so correlated latency/saturation in api-gateway, redis-cache, user-db or ledger-db in the 14:00–14:02Z window is unknown.

Config/telemetry for the identity log pipeline is unreachable: get_config_changes(service='logging') returned not_found and 'logging' is absent from known_services, so the shared-cause hypothesis (H4) is untested, not disproven.

Historical search is keyword-scored (match_score 1–6) with no free-text/exact-phrase control and a small corpus, so closer precedents (e.g. certificate expiry, partial-fleet auth failures) may exist but were not surfaced; the precedent set is a lower bound.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Per-replica error-rate data showing failures confined to a replica subset holding one key id would strongly confirm H1; a uniform failure rate across all replicas with the same key id would argue against H1 and toward H2.

auth-service logs (once the pipeline is restored) showing JWKS/key-load or key-not-found errors for k-2026-04 would confirm H1; showing claim/clock-skew/parse rejections on well-formed tokens would confirm H2.
Reverting only cfg-2705 and seeing the error rate return to baseline within one bucket would confirm H1; no change after that revert but resolution after rolling back dep-5710 would confirm H2.
A per-caller breakdown showing the ~36% failures concentrated in one caller, or a matching api-gateway routing deploy at ~14:00Z, would promote H3 and change the owner of the fault.
Evidence of correlated failures/latency on redis-cache or user-db at 14:00–14:02Z, or a client-side token-format change, would shift support toward H3.
Discovery of a shared credential/secret/network change affecting both log shipping and key distribution (or a direct log-pipeline fault coincident with 14:00Z) would revive H4.
NTP/clock-drift evidence on a subset of auth-service nodes, or a rise in latency/CPU/restarts that the current flat series does not show, would revive H5 and overturn the 'no resource fault' reading.
